claims.text: Equimolar WTaTiVZr has greater high-temperature plastic strain than commercially pure tungsten.
Equimolar WTaTiVZr has greater high-temperature toughness than commercially pure tungsten.
Commercially relevant pure tungsten has very low fracture toughness and brittle transgranular and intergranular failure regimes.
The WTaTiVZr alloy is a homogeneous single-phase BCC material.
The proposed initial WTaTiVZr state contains no significant secondary-phase precipitates.
WTaTiVZr is composed of refractory, reduced-activation elements.
Near-equimolar mixing and atomic-size mismatch produce strong local lattice distortions in WTaTiVZr.
Lattice distortions in WTaTiVZr reduce the Peierls barrier and the activation barrier for dislocation nucleation and motion.
Plastic deformation in TaTiVWZr can be dislocation dominated and thermally activated.
Lower barriers in WTaTiVZr activate additional slip systems, including cross-slip.
Additional dislocation glide and slip delay crack initiation and propagation relative to pure tungsten.
A temperature range of 1000–1600 °C is service-relevant for plasma-facing-component testing.
WTaTiVZr will have lower high-temperature yield stress than pure tungsten because of enhanced dislocation mobility.
WTaTiVZr will show greater dislocation activity and more multi-slip deformation than pure tungsten.
The proposed mechanism applies only while WTaTiVZr remains homogeneous and single-phase BCC.
Secondary-phase formation or precipitate instability may mitigate or alter the proposed plasticity mechanism.
Identical processing and mechanical-test histories make alloy composition and structure the sole causes of any measured difference between WTaTiVZr and pure tungsten.

contradictions.description: The experiment and stated validity boundary are restricted to inert atmospheres, but the prediction is generalized to plasma-facing service conditions, which include exposure to hydrogen isotopes, helium, energetic particles, and neutrons. An inert test does not reproduce that environmental scope.
